global_attributes.title: Climlab aerosol injection run diagnostics
global_attributes.averaging_period: Mean over last 12 monthly time steps

variables.tracer_density: kg kg-1 aerosol mass mixing ratio (inj_pres, inj_lat, cores, lat, lev), yearly mean over last 12 months

selection.combination: sum of the two single-latitude fields (linear transport), equal injection rates

transport_field.altitude_assignment: z(lev) by linear-in-ln(p) interpolation of the US Standard Atmosphere (saimon.atmosphere.us_standard_atmosphere on a 10-m grid); conc = q * rho_air(z_lev); column = trapz(q, p)/g; total = sum(column * band_area)

normalisation.formula: f(phi,z) = [conc(phi,z)/M_tot] / [rho_air(20 km) / (A_earth * int_{16 km}^{z(30 hPa)} rho_air dz)]
normalisation.meaning: f is the local concentration per unit resident mass divided by that of a globally uniform constant-mixing-ratio layer between 16 km and the 30-hPa level evaluated at 20 km; 1 Tg is set by dividing by M_tot, i.e. the steady-state field is scaled linearly to the quoted resident mass (the model's own steady mass is the lifetime times the injection rate)

interpolation.exact_20km: q interpolated linearly in ln(p) to p(20 km) and multiplied by rho_air(20 km) (load_silica_zonal_2d: conc_a); this is what sz.enhancement / results.json scenarios/* use
interpolation.map_levels: no vertical interpolation: f2d is on the 50 model levels; sigma(phi,z) is interpolated linearly in z from the 0.5-km tangent grid (12-28 km) and linearly in latitude from the GloSSAC 5-deg grid (-77.5..77.5, held beyond)
interpolation.campaign: f at exact 20 km boxcar-smoothed over +-0.7 deg (smooth_over_footprint) then np.interp to event latitudes

limb_path.method: ray tangent at the 20.4656-km level centre, geometric (no refraction) straight line, sampled every 0.25 km up to 45 km altitude; latitude along the ray phi0 +- (x/R) cos(azimuth), folded over the pole; f bilinear in (lat, z) from the archived f2d; shells = the model levels with boundaries at the mid-points (saimon.geometry.tangent_to_slant_paths); first-order: f_eff = f(phi0, z_t) + [tau_f(az) - tau_f(zonal)] / L_tt, i.e. the per-shell f perturbation enters with the shell's chord weight relative to the tangent-shell chord (the retrieved tangent-shell extinction is the slant OD minus the upper shells, with the upper shells at their homogeneous value); full: the recursive onion peel run on the gradient and on the zonal slant integrals, difference added to f(phi0, z_t)

zonal_check.note: the zonal-ray peel itself differs from the point value only through the within-shell vertical variation (a finite-vertical-response effect, see vertical_response), which is removed by differencing

vertical_response.method: triangular response of full width W centred on the 20.4656-km level, f linear in z between model levels

campaign.formula: sigma_camp = (f^T C^-1 f)^(-1/2), C = diag(sigma_e^2) + sigma_c^2 1 1^T, sigma_c = rho_c * sigma_ref; Sherman-Morrison: f^T C^-1 f = S_ff - sigma_c^2 S_f1^2 / (1 + sigma_c^2 S_11), S_ab = sum a_e b_e / sigma_e^2; the homogeneous reference (f = 1) is treated identically; gain = sigma_camp(f=1) / sigma_camp(f).  NOTE: with a strictly common additive component the GLS estimator fits the offset out through the latitude pattern (f varies 0.23-3.8 across events), so the homogeneous reference floors at sigma_c while the structured case does not; the 'eq6_weights_true_cov' entries give the Eq.-(6) independent-weight estimator's actual uncertainty under the same covariance, which does not exploit the pattern against the offset

decision_rule.statement: The expected number of false alarms E[count] = N p is a linear functional of the per-test tail probability and holds for any dependence between the N tests; the familywise probability P(at least one) = 1 - (1-p)^N assumes independence (the union bound N p holds for any dependence but is loose, here saturating at 1).
